title: OpenProposal kernel primitives
description: Stage 4 input: kernel/primitives.yaml. Each primitive is defined once, with the concept it represents, one constraint set, a description, its sources, and test vectors. Spec sources are quoted and digested, so a primitive goes stale when a row it rests on changes. The emitters turn each primitive into one named JSON Schema.

description.description: The published description: what a value means, for someone who receives a payload.

type.description: The JSON type of a value.

concept.description: The concept of `kernel/domains.yaml` the primitive represents: the concept's type, or one of its components. Two primitives with the same structure are distinct when they represent different concepts, whose meanings the domain model states.

locks.description: The locks the primitive is published on. Without it, the primitive is published on every lock. The domain gate fails on a primitive that no document reaches on a lock it is published on.

decision.description: The decision record behind a constraint the sources don't state.

vectors.description: Values the constraint set must accept and must reject. The kernel gate checks each one with a 2020-12 validator that asserts `format`.

showcase.description: The value a reader's example payload shows where the specification's examples give none, such as a realistic UUID or an amount of 18.5, and a second, different one for the second item of a list that holds two. The kernel gate checks each one as it checks a valid vector, and against the primitive's rules.

rules.description: Rules on a value that JSON Schema can't express (type rules § 9). The schema accepts every vector of a rule; the rule rejects the invalid ones.

then.description: An integer primitive whose values are a few named codes states only them: titled const branches, and no range beside them.

constraints.description: The one constraint set, written with the JSON Schema 2020-12 validation keywords the emitter copies as they are. Empty means the type alone, for a primitive that carries a meaning but no constraint.

pattern.description: A regular expression in the ECMA-262 dialect, as JSON Schema 2020-12 requires (core § 6.4), anchored with `^` and `$`. It uses no construct that RE2 or Python `re` reads differently: no lookaround, no backreference, and no `\d`, `\w`, or `\s`. The kernel gate runs each pattern in ECMA-262, Go's RE2, and Python `re`. Python's `$` also matches before a final newline, so the gate writes it `\Z` there, and the conformance vectors include a trailing-newline mutant of each valid vector.

format.description: A format that JSON Schema 2020-12 defines.

oneOf.description: The codes of an integer primitive, each a titled const branch, as an integer-coded vocabulary writes its codes (type rules § 6): a primitive whose values are a few integers, each with a name, such as `IntegerFlag`'s `0` (No) and `1` (Yes).

sources.description: Where the primitive comes from. At least one kind is present.

spec.description: Specification elements, quoted and digested as `npm run cite` prints them.

standards.description: External standards the constraint set follows.

design.description: Sections of this repository's design documents. The kernel gate checks that each heading exists.

section.description: The heading text without its `#` marks.

id.description: `kernel:<primitive>:<token>`. The primitive is the rule's owner.

source.description: Where the rule comes from (type rules § 9): specification elements, quoted and digested; an external standard; or the decision record behind it. The kernel gate checks that a spec source is current on each lock and that a decision exists.

digest.description: The element's digest when the source was written. A different current digest makes the primitive stale.

quote.description: The element's text as `npm run cite` prints it.

locks.description: Lock names the source applies to. Without it, the source applies to every lock.

decisionLocks.description: The locks the decision applies on, where the sources state the constraint on every other lock, such as a daypart's form, which an open PR states and `main` leaves to a decision. Without it, the decision applies on every lock the type is published on.
